title: Oxygen — Passenger Service Units — Conversion to the Twenty-Two Minute Chemical Generator
abstract: Conversion of the passenger service unit oxygen generators to the twenty-two minute duration standard, so that operators flying over high terrain can meet their drift-down profile without installing a gaseous system.

sections.planning_reason: Operators opening routes over high terrain find that the fifteen minute generator duration does not cover the drift-down profile their route analysis requires. The only alternative offered until now was a gaseous system, which costs weight, cabin volume and a servicing infrastructure at every line station. Nine operators requested a longer duration solid generator and two made it a condition of an aircraft order. Aircraft that are not converted cannot be dispatched on the affected routes without an operational restriction.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin replaces the chemical generator core in every passenger service unit with the twenty-two minute item, retaining the existing unit envelope and lanyard mechanism. The distribution manifold accumulator and its upstream filter are replaced with items rated for the longer flow duration. Because the new core runs hotter over the longer duration, the thermal blanket in the unit cavity is extended aft and an additional ceiling panel standoff is fitted.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Make sure that the passenger oxygen system is safetied and that all lanyards are secured. Get access to the passenger service units through the ceiling panels in zones 254 and 265. Remove the generator core from each unit and place it in the approved transport container. Extend the thermal blanket aft in each cavity and fit the additional ceiling panel standoff. Install the twenty-two minute core in each unit and connect the lanyard. Remove the manifold accumulator and install the item D3520114349032 rated for the longer duration. Install the filter D3520117593776 upstream of it. Do a pressure and leak check of the distribution manifold. Do the passenger oxygen system operational test following task AMM-Z-35-20-11-200-031-A, including a sample drop test on two units per zone. Restore the ceiling panels and record the embodiment. The manifold arrangement is on drawings D35201154822 and D35201170600.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 Evo model aircraft not delivered at the twenty-two minute standard. Generators of different durations must not be mixed in one cabin, so the conversion is a whole-aircraft activity.
sections.material_note: Kit K3520-1012-01 is quoted per cabin layout and contains the generator cores, the manifold accumulator, the filter, the blanket extensions and the standoffs. Lead time is sixteen weeks from order.

abstract: Conversion of the passenger service unit oxygen generators to the twenty-two minute duration standard, planned and released one aircraft at a time because a cabin may never carry two generator durations at once.

Extend the thermal blanket aft in each cavity and fit the additional ceiling panel standoff. Install the twenty-two minute core in each unit and connect the lanyard. Every unit in the cabin is converted in the same visit; a cabin left with two durations in it may not be released to service, so the work is scheduled as one aircraft event and not as a zone by zone task. Remove the manifold accumulator and install the item D3520114349032 rated for the longer duration. Install the filter D3520117593776 upstream of it. Do a pressure and leak check of the distribution manifold. Do the passenger oxygen system operational test following task AMM-Z-35-20-11-200-031-A, including a sample drop test on two units per zone. sections.material_note: Kit K3520-1012-01 is quoted per cabin layout and contains the generator cores, the manifold accumulator, the filter, the blanket extensions and the standoffs. Lead time is sixteen weeks from order. Because the conversion is a whole-aircraft event, order and slot the kit per aircraft rather than per fleet tranche. Generators are dated stock with a fifteen year life, so align each aircraft with its own scheduled generator replacement: an aircraft converted early scraps the remaining life of every core in the cabin, and that is the largest single cost in the campaign.

type_data.compliance_time: At the operator's convenience, planned one aircraft at a time and normally aligned with that aircraft's scheduled generator replacement.
